items.title: Jensen Huang was a busted flush at Nvidia – he had to go | Nils Pratley
items.summary:
CEO was viewed as ‘irreplaceable’, but recklessness of affair with a woman regarded by US officials as a Chinese spy made him a political liability

Half the tech world made up its mind before the facts could be assessed properly. Jensen Huang was “irreplaceable”, said the chorus at the start of this week. Nvidia would melt without the co-founder’s brilliance, apparently. The chipmaker’s board had to find a way to save its genius for the sake of corporate America and the entire AI universe.

It was always nonsense because, after the passage of only a few days since his confession of infidelity, Huang looked less like a towering corporate titan and more like a political liability.

Continue reading...

Claude chatbot developer had been reported to be aiming for $2tn IPO on Wall Street before investors cooled on AI

Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4tn (£1.1tn) in its imminent stock market flotation, short of the $2tn that had been expected before investors started to question the durability of the AI boom.

The developer of the Claude chatbot was widely reported to be targeting a $2tn initial public offering on Wall Street but its sights have been set lower, according to a US regulatory filing on Tuesday.

items.title: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’
items.summary:
Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes

Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.

Continue reading...
items.t: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’

items.title: Nvidia’s value tumbles after ‘honeytrap’ investigation launched, as China denies spying claims – as it happened
items.summary:
Shares in world’s most valuable company hit seven-month low after CEO Huang admits to affair, after allegations of relationship with Chinese spy

  • Silicon Valley and Trump rally behind Nvidia CEO after his affair with alleged Chinese spy

  • Who is Alice Huang, the woman linked to Nvidia’s CEO?

  • The AI poster boy, the ‘Chinese spy’ and Trump: how an affair may have harmed US security

Huang is receiving support from some fellow tech executives, including Elon Musk.

Musk commented “I agree” on a post by ​Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire that said Huang “did something incredibly dumb” that was “bad for America” but that “Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership”.

“While Nvidia has sought to reassure us all, ​there are several layers here, beginning with the unfortunate timing.

“For example: The company is systemically important for tech, markets and the economy; Investors tend to struggle to price in key-person and governance issues; and there are fluid national security and geopolitical dynamics.”
